entities.summary: Anna Blackburne was an English botanist, naturalist, and collector who assembled an extensive collection of natural history specimens and corresponded with several notable naturalists of her era. Blackburne was born at Orford Hall, Orford, Warrington, Lancashire, into a family of landowners and merchants. After her mother's death, she lived at Orford with her father John Blackburne, who was known for his interest in botany and his hothouses for exotic plants. John Blackburne also had an extensive library where Anne probably studied botany; she later taught herself Latin so she could read the Systema Naturae of Carl Linnaeus.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent English botanist and naturalist, Anna Blackburne's contributions to the field of taxonomy and her extensive collection of specimens helped lay the groundwork for future botanical research. Her work with Carl Linnaeus also highlights the importance of women in scientific collaboration during the Early Modern era.
